headline: Private Lake Access and Forest Adventure Passes
reservation: Lake Arrowhead is a private lake; water access is restricted to property owners and their guests or commercial tour passengers. Public recreation requires a San Bernardino National Forest Adventure Pass for parking at designated trailheads. Accommodations in the Tudor-style village should be secured months in advance for winter holidays or summer weekends.

days.title: Alpine Village and Waterfront
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Lake Arrowhead Village

stops.name: Arrowhead Queen Tour Boat
stops.detail: Take a narrated tour to view the private shoreline and historic architecture of the mountain estates.

stops.name: Lake Arrowhead Village Boardwalk
stops.detail: Walk the waterfront shops and enjoy the Tudor-inspired mountain atmosphere.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour from San Bernardino; steep grades on Highway 18
days.note: Winter travel frequently requires snow chains; check Caltrans R-levels before departing.

days.title: San Bernardino Forest Canopy

stops.name: Heaps Peak Arboretum
stops.detail: Follow the Sequoia Trail loop to learn about native mountain flora and bird species in a protected grove.

stops.name: Rim of the World Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive the ridge-top highway for expansive views of the San Bernardino Valley and distant peaks.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes of local driving; conditions vary with weather
days.note: Adventure Passes are required for parking at Heaps Peak and other forest trailheads.

days.title: Mountain History and Peaks

stops.name: Mountain History Museum
stops.detail: Explore exhibits on the logging, ranching, and early tourism history of the San Bernardino Mountains.

stops.name: Strawberry Peak Lookout
stops.detail: Visit the historic fire lookout tower for a 360-degree view of the surrounding national forest.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; some access roads are narrow and unpaved
days.note: Lookout towers may have restricted access during active fire monitoring; check local status.

intel.title: Village and Trailhead Limits
intel.text: Village parking is plentiful but fills during the summer concert series. Forest trailheads like Splinters Cabin have very limited space and require an Adventure Pass displayed.

intel.title: Mountain Topography
intel.text: Expect frequent signal loss along the Rim of the World Highway and inside deep forest canyons. Offline maps are essential for navigating the residential mountain roads.

intel.title: Rim Area Refueling
intel.text: Fuel is available in Blue Jay and Lake Arrowhead, but prices are typically higher than in the valley. Fill your tank in San Bernardino before starting the steep ascent.

intel.title: Weekend Traffic Patterns
intel.text: Highway 18 experiences significant congestion on Friday evenings (upbound) and Sunday afternoons (downbound). Schedule travel during midweek or early mornings to avoid delays.

intel.title: Winter Road Controls
intel.text: Snowfall can trigger mandatory chain requirements even for 4WD vehicles. Carry a set of chains and know how to install them, as mountain weather changes rapidly.

plan.arrival: Arrive at SBD airport and collect a vehicle capable of mountain grades. Stop in San Bernardino for major supplies, then ascend the 'Rim of the World' toward your cabin.
plan.vehicle: A vehicle with high clearance or 4WD is recommended for winter or unpaved forest roads; check rental terms for mountain driving and chain installation policies.
plan.goldenHour: Keller Peak Fire Lookout; sunset views are highly dependent on seasonal visibility and smog levels from the valley below.
